# Lec. 1: income statement analysis ## 

Types of investments: liquidity vs strategic


- Liquidity: bonds, stocks
- Strategic: loans + equity interest in other companies.
- Investment in subsidiaries - operating investments? 
- In fin statements: subsidiaries fully consolidated, associates -> equity method, joint arrangements (joint operator and joint venturer - **clarify these terms**)
- **Associate vs subsidiary** - explain difference. **ANSWER**: associate - significant influence but no control, subsidiary - control. 
- **What if we consolidate associates intead of using equity method?** - *equity method - clarify*. 

**Clarification**: 
Equity requires recording only net assets of the joint company in the balance sheet, as opposed to assets and liabailities.

## Back to classification of activities ## 

- Non core operating activities - ancillary to the core operating activities, ex.: merchandising/fundraising, gains from disposal of players for a football company, royalties for manufacturing company
- **Two types**: ancillary vs financial and investment prop
- Unusual items - non-recurrent items (non underlying, i.e.) - diclosed separately in icnome statements. 

**Rationale**: 

separate unusual from continuos operations 


**Definition**: 

- violate mathcing principle (when income or expense rtelated to events in past years)
- unusual in nature (not common for industry/business)
- infrequent events (ex.: accident, disposal of business\equipment etc.)
- depends on the context of the industry! for instance if litigation is common, neither unusual nor infrequent. 
-OCI items (revaluation from fair value adjustment, complex estimates etc.)
Statement of income -> net income -> othe comprehensive income
- Used when differing valuation affects balance sheet but not reflected in net income (**ex: revaluation**) - but not in all cases (ex: accounting for financial derivatives)

## Current assets/liabilities ##

- accoridng to IAS3, not only overlap with short term (liquidity) OR current (operating) (managerial) - **hybrid definition**, based on time but also length of business cycle
- The definition relies on **realizing within business cycle** or 12 montths after reporting (thats the only overlap)
- professional analaysts use managerial = better!
- Investment properties classified as non current operating assets.

## Cash and Cash equivalents ## 

- classified as non operating

## Ways to analyze th debts

- **net debts** (difference iin total debts/assets), used for modigliani miller (view decomp)
- **net financial position** (total debt - cash - short term fin assets) minus net short term financial debts (used as upper bound on to ebitda ratios, also to define cost of debt $K_d$)
- **net short term fin debt** (short term debt less cash less short term fin assets) , used for assessing the short term perspective

## Current operating liabilities ## 

- Why current? not time, but normal and recurrent operating cycle - if the liability is recurrent, can be short term or long term! **current = recurrent**

## table with current/non current vs operating/non-operating

|  | **Operating** | **Non-operating / financial** |
|---|---|---|
| **Current assets** | **Accounts receivable**<br>Amounts owed by customers for ordinary sales.<br><br>**Inventory**<br>Goods held for sale or production.<br><br>**Prepayments / contract assets** | **Cash and cash equivalents**<br>Cash not needed for the immediate operating cycle.<br><br>**Marketable securities**<br>Short-term bond or equity investments.<br><br>**Interest receivable** |
| **Non-current assets** | **PPE**<br>Factories, machinery, stores, offices used in the business.<br><br>**Right-of-use assets**<br>Leased premises or equipment used in operations.<br><br>**Operating intangibles**<br>Patents, brands, production software. | **Long-term financial investments**<br>Unrelated equity or bond holdings.<br><br>**Loans to third parties**<br><br>**Non-operating real estate**<br>Property held purely for investment. |

## Summary of important metrics from managerial format ##

| Measure | Definition | Formula | Intuition |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Net operating invested capital (NOIC)** | Net capital committed to the firm’s core operations. It excludes financing and non-operating assets. | $NOIC = Operating\ assets - Operating\ liabilities$<br><br>Equivalently:<br>$NOIC = NOWC + Net\ operating\ non\text{-}current\ assets$ | The amount the firm must finance with debt and equity to run the business after accounting for spontaneous operating funding, such as supplier credit. |
| **Net operating working capital (NOWC)** | Net short-term capital tied up in the operating cycle. | $NOWC = Operating\ current\ assets - Operating\ current\ liabilities$<br><br>Typically:<br>$NOWC = AR + Inventory + Other\ operating\ CA - AP - Accrued\ operating\ CL$ | Cash tied up in credit to customers and inventory, net of credit received from suppliers and other operating creditors. An increase in NOWC is a use of cash. |
| **Net financial position (NFP)** | The firm’s net interest-bearing financial debt after deducting financial liquidity. | $NFP = Interest\text{-}bearing\ financial\ debt - Cash - Marketable\ securities$ | The company’s net financial obligation to lenders. A positive NFP means net debt; a negative NFP means net cash. |

# lecture 6: ROI, ROE #


## ROI ## 

- measure of operating efficiency 
- $\text{Operating income}/\text{invested capital}
- **Decomposition**: 

$$ ROI = \frac{operating income}{Net revenues} \times \frac{Net revenues}{Invested capital} = ROS \times Asset \; turnover
$$ 

- Decompositon into **core vs non core**: 


## ROE decomposition: Modigliani-Miller ## 

$$
\mathrm{ROE}
=
\frac{\text{Comprehensive Income}}{\text{Net Equity}}
=
\frac{\text{Operating Income}}{\text{Invested Capital}}
+
\left(
\frac{\text{Operating Income}}{\text{Invested Capital}}
-
\frac{\text{Financial Expenses}}{\text{Total Liabilities}}
\right)
\times
\frac{\text{Total Liabilities}}{\text{Net Equity}}
\times
\frac{\text{Comprehensive Income}}
{\text{Income before Unusual Items and Taxes}}
$$

- Comment: the difference in operating profitability and expenses defines whether the company is profitable (ROE positive)
- Second technical adjustment: we substract total liabilities from total assets to arrive at net results ("clean" from financial income streams). 

## Operating liability leverage ## 

- Prof Penman proposal: use NOPAT (ne operating profit after tax) instead of operating income 
- Decompose NOPAT/Net operating invested capital into NOPAT over gross operating invested capital and diff between nopat ratio and short term borrowing. 
- Operative liability x Short term interest rates are the implicit cost, which are then added to NOPAT
- Interest rate: either market or short term interest expenses/st fin liabilities
- **Modigliani-Miller, ROE decomposition** (explain)
- **special cases**: fin assets exceed fin liabilities, net operating invested capital negative (net operating liabilities exceed net assets)

## Changes in net equity and effects on ROE ##

Changes of net equity depend: 
- on economic performance: net income vs OCI 
- shareholder transactions (buybacks, new insuance)
- acquisitions, changes in ownership with no loss of control, loss of control. 

**what of extreme cases**? 

- if net operating assets negative: use gross operating assets instead! Does not maket sense to use net operating assets in decomposition since multiplied by short term interest rate, adds value! 
- **DCF vs EVA**: 
- From final example: use financial expenses instead on net expenses to arrive to a "good" number

# Lecture 8: Standard cash flow statements #

## Cash and cash equivalents ## 

- short term and highly liquid
- equity shares excluded excpet preferred shares with a specified redemption date 
- marketavle securities are usually classified as financial assets, not cash and cash equivalents 
- bank overdraft may or may not be classified as cash and cash equivalents depending on the logic 

## Classification of flows ##

- same as the general classification logic 

## Cash flow from operating activities: direct vs indirect ## 

- direct: gross receipts disclosed 
- indirect: adjustments from operating profit or loss


## Taxes ##

- usually operating

## Changes in ownership ## 

- we account for the percentage of control times percentage paid in cash + the acquired cash assets. 
- Cash flows from cash-financed acquisition must be reported in investing section

## Non cash ## 

- acquisition of assets by lease or by assuming liabilities
- acquisition by way of equity issue 
- debt to equity conversion

## Forex ## 

- must be shown separately, as a reconciliation item in the consolidated statement of cash flow.
